translation_notes: prefixes: opcua_ns->opcua, RDF->rdf (both module-level literal Namespace() calls, static @prefix).

BASE = Namespace(base_ns) is local-in-a-function like the stratum's target, but base_ns is a PARAMETER, not a literal string: `@prefix` cannot hold it (no interpolation in `<IRI>` -- INSTRUCTIONS.md §1 only documents `{expr}` for `f<...>`, not for the bare `@prefix ex: <IRI> .` form). Used `@prefix base: f<{base_ns}> .` instead, right after the value is known (after g.parse, matching the source line's position) -- the same formatted-IRI escape already used by the sibling AI-SDC__ACRO__..._build_minimal_graph pair in this stratum for an imported (also non-literal) PREFIX constant. Confirmed directly with the transpiler on a minimal repro (function parameter interpolated in `@prefix base: f<{base_ns}> .`, called with two different base_ns values): it resolves the prefix against the value in force at that point in the block, so a parameter works exactly like the AI-SDC import did. This is NOT one of the three escape routes AGENT_BATCH primed for (DefinedNamespace._NS, dict/registry, g.bind) -- BASE never leaves the function as an object, it is used only via `.attr` -- the blocker is purely that the IRI itself is a runtime value, and `f<...>` already covers that case.

Went beyond the stratum's own idiom for the rest of the region (INSTRUCTIONS.md §2, 'toujours la construction la plus specifique'): `for s, p, o in g.triples((None, RDF.type, BASE.BoundMap))` with p/o discarded -> `for s in m{ ?s rdf:type base:BoundMap }` (single projected variable yields a bare term, exactly g.triples' first tuple element); each `g.value(s, BASE.pred)` -> `m{ {s} base:pred ?o }.first()` (trav_single_value's construction), kept as two SEPARATE m{ } (not fused into the outer pattern) precisely because fusing would change cardinality from 'first value or none' to a join, per the pitfall INSTRUCTIONS.md §2 warns about.

fixture.ttl deliberately excludes opcua:String and an unrecognised datatype: both make the region return the bare class `str` as a dict value, and rdfeval.harness.materialise() then tries to iterate `str` itself (`hasattr(str, '__iter__')` is True on the class though `str` is not iterable) -- 'type' object is not iterable, identically for original.py and translated.ldpy. This is a harness limitation on comparing bare Python `type` objects, unrelated to the translation: float/bool/int/None (the other four branches, all exercised) materialise fine. g.namespace_manager.store.namespace(...) and g.parse(...) are left as plain rdflib calls: no island in the vocabulary covers the namespace-manager's own prefix registry or file parsing, and binding_ns/uaentity_ns are supplied directly in driver.py so that unrelated branch is never exercised.

repair.remaining: Rien d'équivalence à juger sur les entrées du dépôt. Pour mémoire : @graph g et @prefix base: font g.bind() sur le graphe lu, et bind (override=True) retire une liaison existante du même IRI ; si un fichier liait binding: ou uaentity: exactement à base_ns, à opcua: ou à rdf:, la traduction sortirait en sys.exit(1) là où l'original continue. Le dépôt ne l'atteint pas (owl2instances.py:729-731 forge `<prefix>bindings/` et `<prefix>entity/`). opcua_ns disparaît du module traduit (names_only_original) ; binding_server.py ne l'emploie que dans la région (ligne 40).

optimization_notes: optimized.py: Graph().parse(...) is chained; the found_* lookups are folded into the two guards (`if not (binding_ns or g.namespace_manager.store.namespace('binding'))`, no side effects), and the dead reassignments of binding_ns/uaentity_ns go with their comment; the triples() loop becomes g.subjects(RDF.type, BASE.BoundMap).

optimized.py: the five-branch if/elif datatype chain becomes a python_types dict built once before the loop, a membership test for the warning and .get(datatype_uri, str). The test is `in`, not a None check, because LocalizedText is None. Dict lookup gives the same result as the == chain for RDF terms: a Literal or BNode never equals a URIRef, and equal URIRefs hash equal. The sys.exit guards, the printed lines and the default stay.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph g` and `@prefix base: f<{base_ns}> .`, `for s in m{ ?s a base:BoundMap }`, the two g.value reads as separate m{ … }.first() (not joined, which would multiply rows), and opcua:Double etc. as the dict keys (prefixed names work as dict keys before `:`).
